newsitem.title: USA: Crown puts new labor proposal on table.
newsitem.headline: Crown puts new labor proposal on table.

text.p: Crown Central Petroleum Corp put a new proposal on the bargaining table on Monday as talks resumed between the company and locked-out union workers at its Pasadena, Texas refinery, officials said.

The company proposed changes in determining seniority at the refinery, one of the two major sticking points in year-long talks aimed at reaching a new three-year pact with the union, a company spokesman said.

But a union source said the proposal was "more of the same" and said talks appeared to remain stalled over company proposals to trim the 270-person workforce and replace some union workers with contractors.
"All they did was diddle with some clerical issues and put the same old proposals on the table," said the union official, who asked not to be named.

Crown locked out union workers at the 100,000 barrel per day refinery in February 1996 after equipment was found vandalized as talks on a new labor pact broke down. The company for the past year has operated the refinery with salaried workers and contractors.
Crown and union negotiators met with a federal mediator for an hour on Monday. No future talks were scheduled.
